newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to raise up to 700 mln marks in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Romania to raise up to 700 mln marks in bonds.

text.p: Romania's Finance Ministry said on Monday it was planning road shows in three European financial centres this month ahead of launching bonds to raise up to 700 million marks.
The bonds will be Romania's first denominated in marks and the ministry's first international raising.
"We'll be in Zurich on May 27, Frankfurt on May 28 and London on May 29," ministry manager Mihai Tanesescu said.
He said lead managers for the issue, estimated at 500 million to 700 million marks, were CS First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. Other details were unavailable.
"We hope to launch the issue early in June, but it all depends on the reaction of the market," Tanasescu said.
In March, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it had received jointly with CS First Boston a mandate to act as bookrunners and lead managers for the Romania's bond issue.

Romania rejoined international capital markets in 1995, after more than a decade of absence, with syndicated loans for the central bank. The central bank also launched the first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year.

In 1996, Romania won its first credit ratings from major agencies. Japan Credit Rating agency awarded it a BB-plus, higher than the BB-minus ratings of Standard and Poor's and IBCA and BA-three from Moody's Investors Service.
The approved ceiling for international loans raised by the central bank and finance ministry this year is $3.2 billion.
The new centrist government, which defeated leftists in elections last November, has announced a tough reform package to right the economy and win international financial support.
The International Monetary Fund approved a $430 million stand-by loan for Romania in April. The World Bank also pledged another $630 million in credits, which await board approval.
Earlier this year, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said his bank planned to raise up to $1.6 billion in 1997. The bank borrowed around $1.4 billion from world markets last year.
Latest data put Romania's total foreign exchange reserves, including some 90 tonnes of gold, at $2.87 billion in March. Romania's medium- and long-term external debt was $6.9 billion last year.
